translation_notes: the textbook case for this stratum: three nested selectors (g.subjects(a, SHACL.NodeShape), then g.objects(shape, SHACL.targetClass), then -- only when the middle value passes a Python filter -- g.objects(shape, SHACL.property)) collapse into ONE `m{ }` with three motifs sharing `?shape`. The Python-level filter (`str(target_class) in classes`) cannot move into the pattern (m{ } has no OPTIONAL/FILTER), so it stays a plain `if` in the loop body, now applied to every row of the join instead of gating whether the third selector even runs.

this changes WHEN the third selector's work happens (always, vs. only for matching target classes) but not WHAT gets called: rows where the filter fails are simply skipped after materialising, same as `continue` would skip them before. No extra process_property_shape call is introduced because that call only ever depended on (shape, target_class, prop_shape) triples that already satisfied all three motifs.

`SHACL` is a runtime parameter, not a fixed namespace, so the predicate positions use `{SHACL.NodeShape}` / `{SHACL.targetClass}` / `{SHACL.property}` interpolation rather than @prefix -- confirms interpolation works in predicate position inside m{ }, not just object position (the reference's examples only showed the latter).
context shim `context_shim.py`: ClassInfo, PropertyInfo and process_property_shape are called by the region but defined ~1600 lines away in the same file; reproduced unmodified.

fixture exercises: a shape with 2 target classes x 2 property shapes (the join's Cartesian product on a shared subject), a target class absent from `classes` (Python filter, not m{ }, excludes it), a shape with a matching target class but zero property shapes (zero-solution case), and two one-motif-only neighbours (a NodeShape with properties but no targetClass, and a targetClass/property-bearing resource that is not a NodeShape) -- neither contributes a call, which is what proves the join joins.
